title: CEO Interview with Brett Walker of Electroninks
gist: Electroninks CEO Brett Walker pitches particle-free metal-organic decomposition (MOD) inks as an additive, vacuum-free alternative to sputtering/PVD and electroless plating for advanced-package EMI shielding, backside metallization for AI/HPC chips, and copper seed layers. Claims include >99% less power and water than sputtering, up to 100% sidewall coverage vs ~40% for PVD, up to 50% lower cost per package (Savansys modeling), and a Merck KGaA partnership on backside metallization.

themes.theme: Additive metallization vs PVD and plating

insights.claim: Electroninks argues advanced-package metal is today typically deposited by electroless plating or physical vapor deposition, which require large equipment, significant floor space and demanding process chemistry, whereas its MOD inks cure at low temperature in ambient environments without vacuum equipment.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: An additive, vacuum-free metallization route could threaten demand for PVD/sputter tools in back-end packaging.
insights.quote: Today that metal is typically deposited by electroless plating or physical vapor deposition, which bring large equipment, significant floor space and demanding process chemistry.

insights.claim: For EMI shielding, Electroninks claims its spray process uses more than 99 percent less power and water than sputtering, and eight spray coaters fit in the floor space of one PVD system.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Large energy, water and footprint savings could appeal to OSATs facing capex and sustainability pressure.
insights.quote: our spray process uses more than 99 percent less power and water than sputtering, and eight spray coaters fit in the floor space of one PVD system
insights.locator: When most advanced thin film metals

insights.claim: Because sputtering is line-of-sight and Electroninks' process is not, it claims up to 100 percent package sidewall coverage versus about 40 percent for PVD, and third-party modeling by Savansys indicates up to 50 percent lower cost per package.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A claimed 50% cost-per-package reduction in EMI shielding is a meaningful lever for packaging cost structures.
insights.quote: Third-party modeling by Savansys indicates up to 50 percent lower cost per package.

insights.claim: Electroninks' EI-1207 silver ink cures at 160°C and its recon-free process coats sidewalls well enough to remove the dicing and reconstitution steps sputtered films normally require, with reported shielding of 60 dB at 1.2 micrometers and 80 dB at 3 micrometers across 1 to 40 GHz.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Eliminating process steps simplifies packaging flows and could lower OSAT cycle time and cost.
insights.quote: We have reported shielding of 60 dB at 1.2 micrometers and 80 dB at 3 micrometers across 1 to 40 GHz.
insights.locator: In EMI shielding, our EI-1207 silver ink

insights.claim: Electroninks' inks can be applied with existing spray, screen, inkjet and spin-coating equipment, so they plug into infrastructure customers already have, with high material utilization since silver ends up on the product.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Drop-in compatibility lowers adoption barriers versus processes needing new capital equipment.
insights.quote: the silver ends up on the product, not lost in the process
insights.locator: Our inks can be applied with existing

insights.claim: Electroninks acknowledges silver can discolor under heat or humidity testing, but says the change is cosmetic, does not affect conductivity or shielding, and can be addressed through chemistry changes or an overcoat.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Flags a known qualification hurdle for silver ink adoption that buyers will scrutinize.
insights.locator: In EMI shielding, our EI-1207 silver ink

themes.theme: Thermal and backside metallization for AI chips

insights.claim: Heat dissipation is now a design constraint for AI and high-performance computing chips, and conventional sputtering and plating for backside metallization raise cost, equipment, panel-scaling and environmental issues.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI chip thermal demands create a new materials opportunity in backside metallization for packaging suppliers.
insights.quote: backside metallization for AI and high-performance computing chips, where heat dissipation is now a design constraint
insights.locator: The same logic applies to backside

insights.claim: Electroninks is working with Merck KGaA on backside metallization, where a spin-coated MOD layer bonds reliably with thermal interface materials and can replace multilayer metal stacks; the technology is being commercialized at customer sites globally and the companies plan to market it jointly in the US and Asia Pacific.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A Merck KGaA partnership gives a small materials startup channel reach into AI-chip thermal packaging.
insights.quote: A spin-coated MOD layer bonds reliably with thermal interface materials and can replace multilayer metal stacks
insights.locator: In thermal management, we are working

insights.claim: Electroninks launched a copper MOD ink in September 2024 for seed layers, and in June 2026 introduced an air-curable version that cures in open air at about 150°C in 5 to 10 minutes without inert gas or vacuum, positioned as a lower-cost alternative to silver and gold for large-area metallization.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Air-curable copper could displace costlier precious-metal inks and suits panel-level packaging scale-up.
insights.quote: It cures in open air at about 150 degrees Celsius in 5 to 10 minutes, without inert gas, vacuum equipment or specialty tooling.

insights.claim: Electroninks intends its copper MOD ink to displace electroless copper plating and PVD tie layers in seed layers for fine-line metallization and redistribution layers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: RDL seed-layer substitution would extend the threat to incumbent plating chemistry and PVD tooling in advanced packaging.
insights.locator: We also see opportunities in seed layers

insights.claim: Electroninks is using AI-guided research with Citrine Informatics to improve its particle-free silver ink for aerosol jet printing and plans to extend the approach to gold and copper inks.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: An example of AI-accelerated materials development in the semiconductor supply chain.
insights.locator: We are also using AI-guided research

insights.claim: Electroninks was selected in July 2026 for an AFWERX SBIR contract to advance its CircuitJet on-demand PCB manufacturing platform, following a 2021 Phase II SBIR with the Air Force Rapid Sustainment Office, and has an MOU with LIG Nex1 on lightweight, lower-cost antenna materials.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Defense contracts provide non-dilutive funding and a point-of-use manufacturing niche.
insights.locator: We also see opportunities in defense.

insights.claim: Many Indian packaging lines are greenfield builds, giving customers a rare opportunity to design next-generation shielding and metallization processes in from the start; Electroninks participates in India's national IDSPS program with distributor Baba Fine Chemicals.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: India's greenfield packaging buildout may favor new process technologies over incumbent PVD-based flows.
insights.quote: Many Indian packaging lines are greenfield builds, which gives customers a rare opportunity to design next-generation shielding and metallization processes in from the start.

insights.claim: As system-in-package and heterogeneous integration spread, customers need shielding and metallization that can be applied selectively without adding capital equipment or process steps.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Heterogeneous integration growth expands the addressable market for selective, additive metallization.
insights.locator: Packages are also getting more compact

insights.claim: Electroninks' work with SIIX in Japan starts with prototype trials of spray-coated EMI shielding on complex geometries such as automotive control units, and it also sells via Insulectro.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Automotive electronics is an early application channel for spray-on shielding.
insights.locator: Our work with SIIX, for example
